title: Webhooks
content:
# Webhooks

The webhook events a Microsoft account sends for new mail, calendar changes, OneDrive changes and contact syncs, and how Zernio keeps Graph subscriptions alive.

Zernio creates Microsoft Graph change notification subscriptions for every granted area when the account connects. You receive them as ordinary Zernio webhooks: subscribe with `POST /v1/webhooks/settings` and the event names below.

## Events a Microsoft account sends

| Event | Area | When it fires |
|-------|------|---------------|
| `message.received` | `email` | New mail arrives in the inbox |
| `message.sent` | `email` | Mail is sent, through the API or from the user's own mail client |
| `conversation.started` | `email` | The first message of a new thread is stored |
| `calendar.event.created`, `calendar.event.updated`, `calendar.event.deleted` | `calendar` | An event on the user's calendar changes |
| `file.created`, `file.updated`, `file.deleted` | `files` | A file in the user's OneDrive changes |
| `contact.updated`, `contact.deleted` | `contacts` | The contact sync adds, changes or removes a contact |
| `account.rate_limited` | `email` | The mailbox enters a sending cooldown |
| `account.disconnected` | any | Microsoft refused to renew the account's access (the user revoked it or it expired). Carries `reasonCode: "auth_failed"` and `reconnectUrl` |
| `email.sent` | `email` | A mail left through the email API, once per mail, with its `source` |
| `email.opened` | `email` | A message sent with `trackOpens` is opened |
| `email.link_clicked` | `email` | A link in a message sent with `trackLinks` is followed |
| `email.thread_replied` | `email` | Someone writes in the thread of a message sent with `trackReplies` |
| `email.send_failed` | `email` | A scheduled email could not be sent at its time |
| `email.bounced` | `email` | A mail the mailbox sent bounced, once per failed recipient |
| `email.updated` | `email` | A message was read, starred or flagged, labelled, archived, trashed or moved |
| `email.deleted` | `email` | A message was deleted for good |

Every payload carries `account` with `accountId`, `profileId`, `platform: "microsoft"` and `username`.

Calendar, file and contact events add the changed object's `id` and `changeType`: fetch it with the matching endpoint to get its current state.

Calendar events also carry `calendarId` (`primary` for the default calendar) and `masterEventId` for an occurrence of a series. Both are null for a deleted event, which Outlook no longer describes.

The [Inbox webhooks](/webhooks/inbox) page has every payload.

## Read the mail behind a notification

`message.received` comes from the [inbox](/messages/list-inbox-conversations): the email lands as a message in a conversation, one per Outlook conversation, with the subject, `cc` and other email fields under `metadata.email`. Reply from the inbox or with `POST /v1/email/messages/{messageId}/reply`.

## Check push health

`GET /v1/accounts/{accountId}/health` reports `push` for the account:

| Value | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `active` | Push subscriptions are live |
| `pending` | A subscription is not registered yet. Zernio retries within six hours |
| `failed` | Renewal failed three times in a row. Zernio retries once a day |
| `not_applicable` | The account has neither `email` nor `calendar` |

## How it behaves

- Mail notifications cover the Inbox and Sent Items. Zernio then reads the change from Graph, since Graph notifications carry no content.
- `email.updated` carries the message as it is now, with `changes: null`: Graph says a message changed, not what. Moving mail out of the Inbox is `email.updated` with its new `folder`.
- Mail sent from Outlook itself arrives as `message.sent`. Mail sent through the API is announced once, as before.
- Graph subscriptions last about three days for mail and calendar, and about 29 days for OneDrive. Zernio checks every six hours and renews any that expire within the next 24 hours, so you never renew anything yourself.
- Every notification carries a per-subscription secret that Zernio checks before acting on it.
- Graph can send the same change twice. Messages are stored once, but key your own handling on the object `id` too.
- Mail that arrived while push was down is caught up. This runs when Graph reports missed notifications, when it drops a subscription, and when the account reconnects.
- A catch-up lists the Inbox from the last notification, up to 72 hours back. It sends `message.received` only for messages Zernio had not stored.
- Graph's lifecycle events (missed notifications, a removed subscription, reauthorization) are handled for you.
- Contact events come from a sync every 15 minutes, not from push, so they arrive up to 15 minutes after the change.
